findings.message: AC-4 says the second line is the furthest environment the release is in *now*. The `stage` subquery only leaves out voided deployments, so a deployment with status 'rolled-back' still counts as the release being in that environment. Fix: add `and d.status <> 'rolled-back'` (or keep only 'deployed'/'testing'). Add a table test that seeds a rolled-back deployment, since the current tests only exercise `computePortfolio` with a stage already given.
findings.scenario: v0.14.0 is deployed to Staging and then rolled back, with no other deployment. Expected: 'v0.14.0' over 'not deployed'. The Portfolio shows 'v0.14.0' over 'in Staging'.

findings.message: The at-risk rule treats `p.updated_at` as 'last changed'. But the spec-sync upsert (services.ts:344) sets `updated_at = now()` on every sync of a proposal, even when its phase, tasks and meta are the same. Any re-push of a stuck change (a full resync, or a push that resends its folder) resets the 14-day clock, so the project reads on-track. Fix: use a timestamp that only moves when the proposal really changes (for example the latest task-done date or a phase-change time), or make the sync leave `updated_at` alone when nothing changed.
findings.scenario: AMX-090 has been in `building` with no task progress for 30 days. A full resync re-sends its folder unchanged. Health goes from 'At risk: AMX-090 unchanged for 14+ days' to 'On track'.

findings.message: AC-8 asks for unit tests of each rule's branches from AC-1 to AC-6. There is no test for AC-6 ('No manager' for a null manager). The AC-2 'Nothing open' branch in ProjectsPage is never rendered in a test. The e2e checks only AMX's Margin and Manager cells, not its computed Sprint, Health or Next release. Add those cases.
The `list_projects` description names `healthReason` but not `nextReleaseNote` or `openProposals`, which the tool now returns and AC-4 names. Add them so agents know these fields exist.

T1 says Progress reads 'N of M tasks'. Amendment 1 and the code use 'N of M'. AC-3 asks for the reason as `sr` text, but the code shows it as a visible `<small>` plus a `title`. Bring the task text in line with what shipped.

Next release takes the newest release with no live Prod deployment, among all of them. An older release that was never promoted, because a newer one superseded it, is still not in Prod. After the newer one ships, the older one becomes "next" for good. Fix: only consider releases created after the project's newest live-Prod release, or exclude releases older than it.
findings.scenario: v0.13.0 reached Staging and was abandoned. v0.14.0 was created later and released to Prod. No newer release exists → the AMX row shows Next release "v0.13.0 / in Staging", and the lede says "amax is on track for v0.13.0", a version that was already superseded.
